questions.prompt: A podcast titled Learning Lab has an episode titled How City Libraries Support Teen Study Groups, hosted by Samira Cole and released August 15, 2024. Its URL is https://www.learninglab.org/episodes/city-libraries. Using MLA 9 and identifying Cole by the role of host, select the properly formatted entry.
choices: Cole, Samira, host. "How City Libraries Support Teen Study Groups." Learning Lab, 15 Aug. 2024, https://www.learninglab.org/episodes/city-libraries
Cole, Samira. "How City Libraries Support Teen Study Groups." Learning Lab, 15 Aug. 2024, https://www.learninglab.org/episodes/city-libraries
Cole, Samira, host. "How City Libraries Support Teen Study Groups." Learning Lab, Aug. 15, 2024, https://www.learninglab.org/episodes/city-libraries
Samira Cole, host. "How City Libraries Support Teen Study Groups." Learning Lab, 15 Aug. 2024, https://www.learninglab.org/episodes/city-libraries
questions.explanation: MLA 9 presents the host first with the name inverted and the role identified, followed by the episode title, podcast title, and day-month-year date.
questions.topic: Research Skills: Source Evaluation through Citation: MLA and APA

questions.prompt: A webpage by Jonah Kim titled How Noise Pollution Affects Urban Bird Songs appears on Habitat Journal, dated May 12, 2023, at https://habitatjournal.example/noise-birds. Which entry follows APA 7 for a reference list?
choices: Kim, J. (May 12, 2023). How noise pollution affects urban bird songs. Habitat Journal. https://habitatjournal.example/noise-birds
Kim, J. (2023, May 12). "How noise pollution affects urban bird songs." Habitat Journal. https://habitatjournal.example/noise-birds
Kim, J. (2023, May 12). How noise pollution affects urban bird songs. https://habitatjournal.example/noise-birds
Kim, J. (2023, May 12). How noise pollution affects urban bird songs. Habitat Journal. https://habitatjournal.example/noise-birds
questions.explanation: APA 7 uses the date year, month day, sentence case for the webpage title, and the site name before the URL.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 7 of 9: Source Evaluation through Citation (MLA and APA)

questions.prompt: In APA 7, a student directly quotes page 17 of a 2022 book by Elena Brooks and Samuel Ortiz. Which in-text citation is correct?
choices: (Brooks & Ortiz, 2022, p. 17)
(Brooks and Ortiz, 2022, p. 17)
(Brooks & Ortiz (2022), p. 17)
(Brooks, & Ortiz, 2022, p. 17)
questions.explanation: APA 7 uses an ampersand between two authors inside parentheses and places p. before the page number in a direct quotation.
questions.topic: Research Skills: Source Evaluation through Citation: MLA and APA

questions.prompt: A website posts a scanned 1912 letter said to have been written by a well-known suffragist. Which evidence would most strongly help establish whether the letter is authentic?
choices: Trace the scan's provenance and compare it with archival catalogs, paper records, and handwriting evidence.
Count independent websites reproducing the scan and treat the number of copies as proof of authenticity.
Match the handwriting only with famous examples online and treat the closest visual match as conclusive proof.
Check whether historians have quoted the letter and treat repeated quotation as proof of its authenticity.
questions.explanation: Documented provenance and comparison with multiple forms of archival evidence provide a stronger basis for authenticity than popularity, visual resemblance, or later quotation.
questions.topic: Research Skills: Source Evaluation through Citation: MLA and APA

questions.prompt: A district report records 15% fewer recorded disciplinary incidents after phones were restricted during class. A separate study based on end-of-year reading scores finds no detectable change. Which conclusion is most defensible?
choices: The two findings together show that phone restrictions improve reading achievement while reducing classroom misbehavior.
The evidence supports a claim about reduced classroom incidents, but it does not demonstrate improved reading achievement.
The evidence supports a claim about improved reading achievement, but it does not demonstrate reduced classroom incidents.
Because the studies measure different outcomes, neither result can inform a judgment about phone restrictions.
questions.explanation: The district report bears on recorded disciplinary incidents, while the second study addresses reading scores and reports no detectable improvement.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 7 of 9: Research Skills - Source Evaluation through Citation (MLA and APA)

questions.prompt: A researcher wants to examine whether volunteering before ninth grade is associated with finishing high school. Which source offers the strongest evidence?
choices: A blog post quoting five alumni who say volunteering helped them graduate
A peer-reviewed longitudinal study using a representative sample and controlling for prior preparation
A program brochure presenting testimonials selected from successful student volunteers
An opinion column comparing graduation rates among volunteer groups without stating its sources
questions.explanation: The peer-reviewed longitudinal study directly measures volunteering before ninth grade, follows students through graduation, and accounts for relevant prior factors.
questions.topic: Research Skills: Source Evaluation through Citation: MLA and APA

questions.prompt: An infographic claims that students in school music programs are 30 percent more likely to graduate on time. Which research step provides the strongest basis for deciding whether to use the claim in a report?
choices: Compare the infographic's wording with several other social media posts that repeat the same statistic
Trace the statistic to the original study and check its sample, methods, and limitations
Treat the statistic as reliable because the graphic names a university
Use the statistic as a fact without checking whether the study used a representative sample
questions.explanation: Tracing the claim to the original study and examining its sample, methods, and limitations reveals whether the evidence actually supports the infographic's assertion.
questions.skill: Evaluating the evidence behind a statistic
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 7 of 9: Source Evaluation through Citation (MLA and APA)

questions.prompt: A researcher needs a secondary source that interprets how 1960 television audiences understood the presidential debates. Which source best fits?
choices: A 2008 journal article interpreting archived viewer letters and broadcast ratings
A 1960 network memorandum outlining the debate schedule and rules
A 1960 viewer letter describing reactions to the first debate
A 1960 television script prepared by the debate moderators
questions.explanation: The 2008 article interprets original audience evidence and therefore functions as a secondary source.
questions.topic: Research Skills: Source Evaluation through Citation: MLA and APA

questions.prompt: A chapter by Sofia Marin titled Urban Trees and Summer Temperatures appears in Green Cities, edited by Liam Chen and Amara Okafor and published in 2022 by Harborview Press on pages 145–168. Which entry follows APA 7 for a reference list?
choices: Marin, S. (2022). Urban trees and summer temperatures. In L. Chen & A. Okafor (Eds.), Green cities (pp. 145–168). Harborview Press.
Marin, S. (2022). Green cities (pp. 145–168). In L. Chen & A. Okafor (Eds.), Urban trees and summer temperatures. Harborview Press.
Marin, S. (2022). Urban trees and summer temperatures. In Green cities (L. Chen & A. Okafor, Eds.; pp. 145–168). Harborview Press.
Marin, S., Chen, L., & Okafor, A. (2022). Urban trees and summer temperatures. In Green cities (Eds.) (pp. 145–168). Harborview Press.
questions.explanation: An APA chapter reference begins with the chapter author and date, then gives the editors, book title, page range, and publisher in that order.
questions.skill: Formatting an APA edited-book chapter reference
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 7 of 9: Source Evaluation through Citation (MLA and APA)

questions.prompt: A webpage titled Student Robotics Projects is published on the Future Forge website. It has no individual or group author and no publication date. Which APA 7 parenthetical citation is correct?
choices: (Student Robotics Projects, n.d.)
(Future Forge, n.d.)
(Robotics Projects at School, n.d.)
(Student Robotics Projects, 2024)
questions.explanation: Because the work has no author, APA 7 uses its title in the author position, and because no date is available, it uses n.d.
questions.skill: Citing an APA 7 work with no author
questions.topic: Citation: APA 7

questions.prompt: A student wants evidence of how residents reacted to a 1965 city bus strike while it was occurring. Which source is a primary source?
choices: A 2020 history book analyzing the strike's labor negotiations
A 1995 documentary reviewing the strike three decades later
A 2015 museum webpage summarizing the strike's historical impact
Letters sent to a newspaper and published during the strike
questions.explanation: Letters published during the strike are firsthand evidence created while the event was unfolding, so they are primary sources for contemporary reactions.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 7 of 9: Research Skills - Source Evaluation through Citation (MLA and APA)

questions.prompt: A 2011 city report counted only curbside recycling pickups, while a 2024 report also counted materials dropped at recycling centers. Which research practice is soundest before comparing the recycling rates?
choices: Treat the two rates as noncomparable unless both can be recalculated using the same recycling definition.
Estimate the missing 2011 center total from the 2024 total and use that estimate to claim a precise trend.
Use the 2024 rate as the baseline and treat it as the starting point for measuring future change.
Compare the published rates directly because each report uses the label recycling rate.
questions.explanation: Because the reports count different forms of recycling, a valid comparison requires consistent definitions or an explicit acknowledgment that the rates are not directly comparable.
questions.topic: Research Skills: Source Evaluation through Citation: MLA and APA

questions.prompt: Lena Ortiz wrote a webpage titled The History of the Pencil for the Museum of Design. The page was published on 3 May 2022 at https://museum.example.edu/pencil. Which entry follows MLA 9 for the works-cited list?
choices: Ortiz, Lena. "The History of the Pencil." Museum of Design, 3 May 2022, https://museum.example.edu/pencil.
Ortiz, Lena. The History of the Pencil. Museum of Design, May 3, 2022, https://museum.example.edu/pencil.
Ortiz, Lena. "The History of the Pencil." 3 May 2022, Museum of Design, https://museum.example.edu/pencil.
"The History of the Pencil." Ortiz, Lena. Museum of Design, 3 May 2022, https://museum.example.edu/pencil.
questions.explanation: MLA 9 places the author first, uses quotation marks for a webpage title, identifies the website after it, gives the date in day-month-year order, and includes the URL.
questions.skill: Creating an MLA 9 works-cited entry for a webpage
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 7 of 9: Research Skills—Source Evaluation through Citation, MLA and APA

questions.prompt: Two reputable-looking websites report different percentages for teen screen time, and each number is based on a different survey. Which research step is best before deciding which percentage is more useful?
choices: Choose the percentage from the website that was published most recently, regardless of survey methods
Average the two percentages to produce an estimate that accounts for both surveys
Trace each percentage to the original survey and compare the sampled ages, dates, and measurement methods
Use the percentage from the website with more social-media shares, since public engagement indicates accuracy
questions.explanation: Comparing the original surveys reveals whether differences in populations, timing, or measurement explain the conflicting percentages.
questions.topic: Research Skills: Source Evaluation through Citation: MLA and APA

questions.prompt: A webpage titled How Libraries Support Teen Learning was authored by Maya Chen, dated 4 March 2024, and published on the City Education Portal at www.cityed.gov/teen-learning. Which entry follows MLA 9 for the works-cited list?
choices: "How Libraries Support Teen Learning." Maya Chen, 4 Mar. 2024, City Education Portal, www.cityed.gov/teen-learning.
Chen, Maya. How Libraries Support Teen Learning. City Education Portal, 4 Mar. 2024, www.cityed.gov/teen-learning.
Chen, Maya. "How Libraries Support Teen Learning." City Education Portal, 4 Mar. 2024, www.cityed.gov/teen-learning.
Chen, Maya. "How Libraries Support Teen Learning." 4 Mar. 2024, City Education Portal, www.cityed.gov/teen-learning.
questions.explanation: MLA places the author first, uses quotation marks for the webpage title, and gives the container, date, and URL in that order.
questions.topic: Research Skills: Source Evaluation through Citation: MLA and APA

questions.prompt: A manuscript by Lena Ortiz titled Remote Work and Adolescent Time Management has not been peer reviewed. It was posted in 2024 to the Midtown University Research Repository and assigned DOI https://doi.org/10.1234/mu.2024.017. Which APA 7 reference-list entry is correct?
choices: Ortiz, L. (2024). [Preprint] Remote work and adolescent time management. Midtown University Research Repository. https://doi.org/10.1234/mu.2024.017
Remote work and adolescent time management [Preprint]. (2024). Ortiz, L. Midtown University Research Repository. https://doi.org/10.1234/mu.2024.017
Ortiz, L. (2024). Remote work and adolescent time management [Preprint]. Midtown University Research Repository. https://doi.org/10.1234/mu.2024.017
Ortiz, L. (2024). Remote work and adolescent time management. Midtown University Research Repository [Preprint]. https://doi.org/10.1234/mu.2024.017
questions.explanation: APA 7 identifies a manuscript posted in a repository as a preprint and places that descriptor immediately after the title.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 7 of 9: Research Skills - Source Evaluation through Citation (MLA and APA)

questions.prompt: Ana Torres and Ben Wu edited Digital Citizenship Across Classrooms, published in its second edition by Routledge in 2022. Which reference-list entry follows APA 7?
choices: Torres, A., & Wu, B. (Eds.). (2022). Digital citizenship across classrooms (2nd ed.). Routledge.
Torres, A., & Wu, B. (2022). Digital citizenship across classrooms (2nd ed.). Routledge.
Torres, A., & Wu, B. (Eds.). Digital citizenship across classrooms (2nd ed.). (2022). Routledge.
Torres, A., & Wu, B. (Eds.). (2022). Digital citizenship across classrooms (3rd ed.). Routledge.
questions.explanation: APA 7 uses (Eds.) after the editors' names, places the publication year immediately after that element, and includes the edition in parentheses after the title.
questions.topic: Tester 7 of 9: Entry Check, Part 7 of 9

questions.prompt: In MLA 9, a paper cites the only work it uses from the World Health Organization: a report titled Mental Health and Teen Screen Use with no page numbers. What belongs in the parentheses?
choices: (World Health Organization)
(World Health Organization n.p.)
(World Health Organization 2024)
(Mental Health and Teen Screen Use)
questions.explanation: MLA 9 uses the corporate author's name for an in-text citation and normally omits the year when only one work by that author is cited.
questions.topic: Research Skills: Source Evaluation through Citation: MLA and APA

questions.prompt: A survey of 50 honors students finds that students who use planners have higher grades. To test whether planner use causes the difference, which follow-up study would provide the strongest evidence?
choices: Survey another 50 honors students about planner use and compare their self-reported grades.

questions.prompt: A master essayist is known for beginning with a definition and then ending with a vivid image. Which sentence best imitates that technique?
choices: Courage means acting despite fear; on a difficult climb, it is the hand that reaches for the next hold.
On a difficult climb, a steady hand reaches for the next hold; courage means acting despite fear.
Courage means acting despite fear, and fear often shapes the choices people make in danger.
A climber's hand reached for the next hold, trembling with fear but refusing to let go.
questions.explanation: The sentence first defines courage and then uses the image of a hand reaching for the next hold to make the idea vivid.
questions.topic: Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A speaker argues that every college should require applicants to submit applications online because paper processing is slow. Which response best combines a possible benefit of online submission with a limitation of the proposal?
choices: Online applications may speed up processing for many students, but a universal requirement could exclude applicants with unreliable internet access.
Online applications may speed up processing for every applicant, so a universal requirement will remove all access problems.
Most technology experts prefer online applications, which proves that every applicant can complete the forms without difficulty.
Paper applications may be inconvenient for some applicants, but requiring online submission will solve the problem for every applicant.
questions.explanation: It pairs a qualified processing benefit with a specific access barrier created by a universal requirement.
questions.skill: Balancing a benefit against a limitation
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: A survey of regular users of a community pool found that 68 percent said exercising there improved their mood. A council member concludes that opening a pool would benefit every resident in the community. Which assessment of the conclusion is most accurate?
choices: Regular users may already value exercise, so the survey does not show that nonusers would benefit from the community pool.
The results show that the community pool improves mood for every resident in the surrounding area.
Because 68 percent of regular users felt better, regular exercise is guaranteed to improve mental health for all participants.
The survey suggests that the community pool benefits residents only when they already exercise regularly.
questions.explanation: The first assessment appropriately notes that the surveyed regular users may differ from the broader population the council member wants to include.
questions.skill: Evaluating the scope of survey evidence
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Evidence and Nuance

questions.prompt: A city council says, We can either build a costly flood barrier or leave the riverside homes unprotected. Which response most accurately identifies the problem with the argument?
choices: It assumes that flood barriers will cost more than any other protective measure.
It presents only two choices even though other protective measures may be possible.
It predicts that riverside homes will remain dry if no barrier is built.
It treats the riverside homes as more valuable than neighborhoods farther inland.
questions.explanation: The argument creates a false dilemma by treating two options as exhaustive when other protective measures could also be considered.
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: A school argues that starting 45 minutes later will help students sleep more and focus better in class. Which objection most directly challenges the argument's key assumption?
choices: A later start time would require the district to pay for additional transportation.
Starting 45 minutes later may not improve sleep if students continue going to bed at their usual times.
Some families would prefer the school to keep its current start time.
Bus schedules and bus routes would need to be adjusted to accommodate a later start.
questions.explanation: This objection identifies the unstated link between a later start and more sleep, which would not occur if students kept their usual bedtimes.
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: A school board wants to require shared uniforms. Some families say the policy would strain their budgets, and the board is considering providing vouchers. Which response best acknowledges the cost concern while explicitly preserving the policy's consistency benefits?
choices: Although some families may struggle to afford uniforms, district vouchers could reduce that cost while maintaining the consistency of students' clothing.
Uniforms may reduce the time students spend choosing clothes, but families will probably object to the district's plan.
District vouchers would be expensive, so the school should abandon its shared-uniform policy.
A district voucher program could make uniforms affordable for families who need financial assistance.
questions.explanation: The sentence recognizes the financial burden, answers it with vouchers, and retains the policy's benefit of making students' clothing more consistent.
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: A writer states, "The program attracted many applicants, and the committee selected only eight." Which conclusion is fully supported by this information?
choices: The program received a large number of applications but limited the number selected.
The program was so popular that every applicant received an offer of admission.
The committee chose the eight strongest applicants from the entire pool.
The program's low selection rate proves that its standards were unreasonable.
questions.explanation: The statement directly supports the conclusion that many people applied while the committee selected only a small number of applicants.
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: A master writer is known for cleft sentences, which single out one element for emphasis. Which sentence best imitates this technique?
choices: The missing safety permit delayed the opening.
The opening was delayed because the safety permit was missing.
It was the missing safety permit that delayed the opening.
That the permit was missing delayed the opening.
questions.explanation: This cleft sentence isolates the missing safety permit as the cause and gives that element special emphasis.
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance through Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A mayor called a plan a sensible step, although she had opposed every element of it the week before. What is the most likely implication of the sentence?
choices: The contrast between her praise and her earlier opposition creates irony and suggests that her endorsement is insincere.
The public must have been persuaded to support the plan by her recent change of position.
The mayor believed that the opposition had continued for exactly one week.
Other officials agreed with the mayor because she had described the plan positively.
questions.explanation: The juxtaposition of enthusiastic praise with consistent opposition creates irony and implies that the mayor's positive words are not sincere.
questions.topic: Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A writer describes an empty auditorium with this sentence: Sunlight filled the hall, yet every seat remained vacant. Which statement best explains the effect of the description?
choices: The contrast between sunlight and vacancy shows that the writer wants readers to admire the architecture.
The contrast between bright sunlight and vacant seats emphasizes the auditorium's desolation.
The verb filled presents the sunlight as moving rapidly through the empty hall.
The phrase every seat remained vacant uses understatement to minimize the size of the audience.
questions.explanation: The juxtaposition of bright sunlight with vacant seats creates a contrast that intensifies the auditorium's sense of emptiness and desolation.
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance through Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A master writer is known for anadiplosis, the repetition of a sentence's final phrase at the beginning of the next sentence. Which pair of sentences best imitates this technique?
choices: The council opened the hearing. After the meeting, serious gaps appeared in the proposal.
The council opened the hearing. Serious gaps in the proposal appeared after the meeting.
After the council opened the hearing, serious gaps in the proposal appeared.
The council opened the hearing. The hearing exposed serious gaps in the proposal.
questions.explanation: This pair repeats the phrase the hearing at the end of the first sentence and the beginning of the second, demonstrating anadiplosis.
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance through Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A student argues that the school should publish all teacher evaluations. A parent objects that anonymous results may be misleading. Which response best answers the objection while supporting publication?
choices: Publishing the number of evaluations and the rating scale, along with teacher responses, would help readers judge reliability without concealing results.
Publishing only evaluations that exceed a predetermined rating level would protect readers from unreliable anonymous results.
parents should trust every anonymous evaluation because teachers have little incentive to improve without public feedback.
ending teacher evaluations would eliminate misleading results, but it would also remove evidence of instructional quality.
questions.explanation: This response addresses the concern about reliability with relevant information while preserving the student's argument for public access.
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: Polysyndeton is the deliberate repetition of conjunctions within a series of related words or phrases. Which sentence uses polysyndeton?
choices: The committee listened closely. The committee questioned carefully. The committee revised the proposal.
The committee listened and questioned and studied and revised the proposal before voting.
The committee asked for evidence, and the evidence changed its recommendation.
The committee listened carefully, yet it answered cautiously.
questions.explanation: The repeated and conjunctions deliberately separate and connect the committee's four actions, making polysyndeton the defining feature.
questions.topic: Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A writer recommends that a city expand its bus network to reduce traffic. Which sentence most effectively concedes a legitimate concern while preserving the recommendation?
choices: The project's high cost should lead officials to reject it, since reducing traffic matters less than avoiding public spending.
Dependable routes can reduce traffic, so officials should approve the project without weighing its costs or effects on access.
The project may require significant public spending, but dependable routes can give commuters a practical alternative to driving.
Although the project can reduce traffic, it creates no costs or access problems, so officials need not review it before acting.
questions.explanation: It acknowledges the legitimate cost concern while explaining how dependable bus routes can still reduce reliance on private cars.
questions.skill: Conceding a concern while preserving an argument
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: An argument observes that every program funded by the district increased attendance and concludes that every district program will increase attendance. Which criticism most directly identifies the flaw in the conclusion?
choices: The argument assumes that a pattern found among funded programs will hold for every program without showing that the programs are comparable.
The argument assumes that the attendance figures were accurate instead of checking the records used to calculate them.
The argument focuses on attendance rather than examining the district's other educational priorities.
The argument treats attendance as an important goal even though several funded programs served different populations.
questions.explanation: The argument improperly extends a pattern observed in some programs to every program without establishing that their circumstances are sufficiently similar.
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: A study surveyed 120 teenagers and found that those reporting eight or more hours of sleep had higher average scores on one attention test. Which conclusion stays within the scope of the evidence?
choices: In every setting, teens who reported more sleep scored higher on every attention task.
Teens who reported less sleep always performed worse on that test, regardless of other factors.
On that test, teens reporting more sleep had higher average attention scores.
The study proved that more sleep directly caused higher attention scores for all teens.
questions.explanation: This statement stays within the surveyed group and the single test while avoiding claims of universality or causation.
questions.skill: Matching a claim's scope to evidence
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: A city proposes replacing single-use shopping bags with reusable bags to reduce waste. A critic notes that washing reusable bags can use water and energy. Which response most effectively acknowledges that concern while preserving the proposal's environmental benefit?
choices: Because washing reusable bags can use water and energy, cities should require shoppers to use disposable bags instead.
Although washing reusable bags can use water and energy, their environmental benefits are too limited to justify replacing single-use bags.
Although washing reusable bags can use water and energy, replacing several single-use bags over time can still reduce waste.
The concern about washing is reasonable, but cities should require reusable bags without evaluating their total environmental effects.
questions.explanation: This response acknowledges the water and energy cost of washing while explaining why reusable bags can still reduce waste when they replace single-use bags.
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance through Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A principal says that limited funds mean the school must choose between replacing broken textbooks and adding a reading tutor. Which response most effectively challenges the argument?
choices: The principal has not ruled out phased purchases, smaller grants, or other funding sources.
The principal should postpone both plans until the school can afford each one fully.
Textbook replacement matters less because schools can share digital files.
Students need a reading tutor more often than they need current textbooks.
questions.explanation: This response challenges the false dilemma by showing that the school might not have to choose one complete project instead of the other.
questions.topic: Tester 5 of 9: Entry Check, Part 5 of 9

questions.prompt: Researchers found higher average test scores in 20 phone-free classrooms than in 30 phone-permitted classrooms within one district. A school board cites the study to justify a ban in every school. Which response best challenges the board's reasoning?
choices: Because the two classroom groups produced different averages, the study proves that every phone ban will improve scores everywhere.
Results from 30 phone-permitted and 20 phone-free classrooms in one district cannot prove that a ban will improve scores in every school.
The study cannot support any conclusion about phone policies because it examined only 50 classrooms.
Because the study compared two groups within one district, it establishes the same causal effect in every school.
questions.explanation: It correctly limits the evidence to one district instead of treating a limited comparison as proof for every school.
questions.skill: Identifying an overgeneralization in an argument
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: A school reports that students in its robotics program earned better grades after joining, and a board member claims the program caused the improvement. A critic notes that students who choose robotics may already be more motivated. Which response best strengthens the board member's claim?
choices: Compare outcomes for program participants with outcomes for similarly eligible nonparticipants, and ideally assign program places randomly.
Ask participating students whether they believe the robotics program improved their study habits.
Highlight the program's popularity because enthusiastic participation suggests that it benefits students.
Report that program attendance was voluntary while leaving the academic comparison unchanged.
questions.explanation: Comparing similar students and using random assignment when possible would reduce the influence of preexisting motivation on the results.
questions.skill: Evaluating a Rebuttal to an Alternative Explanation
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: A student argues that the school district should add a later bus route. Which response most effectively acknowledges a legitimate concern while preserving the recommendation?
choices: Although an evening route would require added staffing, it could still give students safer transportation after late activities.
Although an evening route would require added staffing, no additional service should be provided without unanimous student support.
Because an evening route would require added staffing, the district should postpone the change until every other route expands.
If evening service requires added staffing, the district should study the issue, though its current schedule should remain unchanged.
questions.explanation: This response concedes the cost of added staffing while showing how the proposed route could still provide an important benefit.
questions.skill: Conceding a concern within a rebuttal
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: A master essayist is known for measured, formal sentences that begin with a concessive clause and end with a specific recommendation. Which sentence best imitates that style?
choices: Early surveys showed that the policy was popular, but its projected costs, uneven benefits, and uncertain long-term effects make careful revision necessary.
The policy was popular in early surveys, and its financial costs, unequal benefits, and possible future effects deserve careful consideration.
Although the policy was popular in early surveys, its projected costs, uneven benefits, and uncertain long-term effects are worth discussing before any decision.
Although the policy was popular in early surveys, its projected costs, uneven benefits, and uncertain long-term effects make careful revision necessary.
questions.explanation: It opens with a concessive Although clause and closes by recommending careful revision, matching the stated formal pattern.
questions.skill: Imitating concessive syntax and formal style
questions.topic: Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A master essayist is known for using a colon to introduce a list that clarifies the main claim. Which sentence best imitates that technique?
choices: The plan failed for three reasons: it cost too much, it arrived late, and it confused riders.
The committee announced its decision: the proposal would proceed after a final review.
The library's hours will expand: students will gain more places to study.
The survey produced one result: respondents preferred online forms.
questions.explanation: The colon introduces a three-part list that explains the claim that the plan failed.
questions.topic: Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A master writer is known for rhetorical questions that begin with an if-clause and challenge claims of fairness. Which sentence best imitates that technique?
choices: If a policy cannot survive the question of who it leaves behind, why should the council call it fair?
A policy that leaves some applicants behind is not equitable, so the council should reconsider the rule before adoption.
Why should the council defend a policy when applicants without reliable internet cannot complete it?
The council cannot honestly describe the policy as equitable if some applicants cannot use the system.
questions.explanation: It opens with an if-clause and turns the fairness claim into a rhetorical question about excluded applicants.
questions.topic: Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A student wants to imitate the brisk, confident tone of a master essayist. Which sentence best demonstrates that tone?
choices: Perhaps the proposal might possibly have some merit, although I remain unconvinced.
The proposal fails on three clear counts, and the evidence leaves no room for doubt.
The proposal raises several interesting questions that deserve further discussion.
The proposal is a proposal, and proposals are proposals, as we all know.
questions.explanation: The direct language, firm assertion, and absence of hedging create the brisk, confident tone the student is aiming to imitate.
questions.skill: Matching tone when imitating a style
questions.topic: Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A master writer is known for long periodic sentences that gather a series of details before placing the main assertion near the end. Which sentence best imitates that technique?
choices: After the team had drafted, revised, tested, and presented the proposal, the chair finally asked for a vote.
The chair asked for a vote after the team presented the proposal.
The team drafted and revised the proposal, and then the chair asked for a vote.
Before the team finished testing the proposal, the chair asked for a vote.
questions.explanation: The introductory sequence delays the key action, and the sentence's main assertion arrives in the final clause.
questions.topic: Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A paragraph begins: We gathered the maps. We checked the supplies. We began the climb. We reached the summit. Which description best explains the effect of repeating We at the start of each sentence?
choices: The repetition emphasizes the group's successive actions and gives the sequence momentum.
The repetition delays the main point until the end of the final sentence.
The repetition reverses the order of two parallel grammatical structures.
The repetition shifts the final words of consecutive sentences into the next.
questions.explanation: The repeated openings emphasize the group's successive actions and create momentum through the sequence.
questions.topic: Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A master writer is known for understatement, describing serious trouble in calm, restrained language. Which sentence best imitates that technique?
choices: The blackout shut down every hospital in the district, though officials called it a minor inconvenience.
The blackout shut down every hospital in the district, and officials called it a catastrophic emergency.
The blackout shut down every hospital in the district, while officials provided a detailed timeline of the outage.
The blackout shut down every hospital in the district, although officials admitted that the entire electrical grid had failed.
questions.explanation: Calling the shutdown of every hospital a minor inconvenience creates understatement by contrasting the scale of the disaster with deliberately mild language.
questions.topic: Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A master essayist is known for opening an abstract argument with a brief comparison and ending with a practical recommendation. Which sentence best imitates that method?
choices: City budgets resemble household budgets because both must balance income and expenses.
A city budget is like a household budget, and both can fail when spending exceeds income.
A city budget is like a household budget: officials should set priorities before expenses grow.
City leaders should study household finances before setting priorities for public spending.
questions.explanation: The sentence begins with a comparison between a city budget and a household budget, then ends with a specific recommendation for officials.
questions.topic: Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A speaker argues that the town should build a new community center. A critic replies that the town's budget is already stretched thin. Which response best addresses the critic's point?
choices: The critic is right, so the town should not build a community center.
If the budget is the obstacle, the town could seek grants or phase the project in stages.
Some residents say they would use a community center if one were built.
The town has never built a community center before, and new buildings are risky.
questions.explanation: This response directly answers the critic's specific objection by offering realistic ways to overcome the budget limitation.
questions.skill: Rebutting an objection with a counterproposal
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: A writer describes a protest as follows: The crowd surged through the square, smashing barriers and overturning benches. Which claim about the writer's diction is best supported by the quotation?
choices: The nouns square and barriers show that the writer wants readers to admire the architecture.
Surged, smashing, and overturning create forceful motion and emphasize the protest's disruption.
Crowd, square, and barriers establish a quiet, ceremonial atmosphere.
Surged conveys deliberate calm, while smashing and overturning conceal physical action.
questions.explanation: The verbs surged, smashing, and overturning depict rapid, forceful actions that make the disruption feel intense.
questions.skill: Analyzing diction for tone and meaning
questions.topic: Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A speaker says, No one can object to the recycling rule because almost everyone supports recycling. Which criticism of the reasoning is most accurate?
choices: The speaker treats broad support for recycling as proof that no reasonable objection to a particular rule exists.
The phrase almost everyone makes the claim mathematically impossible to verify.
Rules are easier to enforce when the people affected by them support the general purpose.
Recycling programs usually create more waste through the packaging they require.
questions.explanation: The criticism identifies that support for recycling in general does not eliminate objections to the details of a particular recycling rule.
questions.topic: Tester 5 of 9: Entry Check, Part 5 of 9

questions.prompt: A speaker says a congestion fee will reduce traffic only if most drivers change their routes. Which response addresses the strongest version of that concern?
choices: Some drivers dislike congestion fees, so the concern about large-scale participation is exaggerated.
Other cities charge congestion fees, so the concern about driver participation is irrelevant.
If driver participation matters, the city should pair the fee with transit discounts and a gradual rollout.
The fee will reduce traffic in every city, even if most drivers ignore it.
questions.explanation: This response takes the participation condition seriously and proposes measures that could meet it.
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: Original sentence: The district initiated a comprehensive initiative to facilitate stakeholder engagement. A master essayist is known for replacing abstract administrative language with specific, observable details. Which revision best follows that approach?
choices: The district held four evening meetings where parents reviewed the new attendance policy.
The district initiated a broad effort to improve stakeholder engagement.
The district began a comprehensive initiative to strengthen stakeholder collaboration.
The district held a meeting for families to discuss school matters.
questions.explanation: The revision replaces abstract phrases with observable details about the number, timing, participants, and purpose of the meetings.
questions.topic: Tester 5 of 9: Entry Check, Part 5 of 9

questions.prompt: A writer wants to make clear that a school board rejected a proposal rather than merely postponing consideration of it. Which revision is most precise?
choices: The board voted down the proposal after hearing several objections.
The board made a decision about the proposal after hearing several objections.
The board reached a conclusion about the proposal after hearing several objections.
The board addressed the proposal after hearing several objections.
questions.explanation: The first revision identifies the board's specific action as voting down the proposal, removing the ambiguity found in the other versions.
questions.topic: Style Analysis: Precise Diction

questions.prompt: A speaker argues that downtown businesses should provide bicycle parking because it would encourage more people to cycle instead of drive. A critic replies that installing racks could cost businesses money and take up space. Which response most effectively addresses the critic's concern while preserving the original argument?
choices: If businesses need financial help, the city could offer grants and allow each business to choose a rack design that fits its available space.
Businesses should be exempted from the bicycle-parking requirement if installation would inconvenience some of their customers.
Providing bicycle racks will increase cycling in every downtown area, regardless of cost or space constraints.
The city should require businesses to install as many bicycle racks as possible, even if some businesses must reduce their floor space.
questions.explanation: The first response acknowledges the practical concern and proposes solutions that could allow the requirement to remain in place.
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: A writer imitates a master's style with this sentence: The rain fell, the wind rose, and the harbor lights vanished one by one. Which description best explains the stylistic effect of the sentence?
choices: The repeated three-part structure creates a steady, cumulative rhythm.
The long list of details makes the scene feel calm and peaceful.
The final phrase uses understatement to suggest the harbor was crowded.
The sentence uses a formal conclusion that sums up the scene's meaning.
questions.explanation: The three clauses follow the same pattern and build one after another, producing a cumulative rhythm that matches the sentence's effect.
questions.topic: Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A master essayist begins with a brief scene and then turns from that experience to a broad claim. Which sentence best imitates that method?
choices: On the first day of term, Maya opened her locker and found a note no one had sent. Curiosity, after all, drives every difficult choice.
Curiosity, after all, drives every difficult choice. On the first day of term, Maya opened her locker and found a note no one had sent.
Because curiosity drives every difficult choice, Maya opened her locker and found a note no one had sent.
Maya opened her locker and found a note no one had sent because she was curious, although she later ignored it.
questions.explanation: The sentence presents a specific scene first and then uses that experience to introduce a broader generalization.
questions.topic: Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A student argues that installing solar panels on the school roof will cut energy costs. A facilities manager says the roof's angle makes the panels ineffective. Which response most effectively acknowledges the concern while addressing the proposal?
choices: Although panels on that roof may produce little power, an energy assessment could determine whether a community solar subscription would work instead.
School officials should disregard the roof assessment because solar energy always reduces costs.
Solar panels are less expensive than every other energy source available to the district.
The district should remove energy costs from the school's budget priorities.
questions.explanation: The response acknowledges the roof's limitation while proposing an assessment and an alternative way to obtain solar energy.
questions.topic: Tester 5 of 9: Entry Check, Part 5 of 9

questions.prompt: A student argues that schools should require a course in financial literacy. A parent objects that the course would take time away from mathematics instruction. Which response most effectively acknowledges the concern while supporting the student's position?
choices: Schools should drop the financial-literacy requirement if any parent objects to the time it requires.
Parents should be responsible for teaching their children about money before high school begins.
Even if a course uses some class time, schools can integrate financial lessons into mathematics and other subjects.
Financial literacy matters less than preserving every minute of mathematics instruction.
questions.explanation: The third response concedes that time is limited while showing how schools can teach financial literacy without creating a separate course.
questions.skill: Conceding a concern without abandoning an argument
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: A nonprofit reports that 74 percent of students who attended all three study workshops later earned better grades. A donor concludes that attending the workshops caused the improvement. Which response most directly challenges that conclusion?
choices: Students who attend three workshops may already be more motivated than other students, so the difference in grades may have existed before attendance.
The donor should require every student to attend all three workshops because most participants reported better grades.
The nonprofit's 74 percent figure is too low to show any connection between workshop attendance and academic performance.
The donor should shorten the workshops so that participating students have more time to study outside class.
questions.explanation: This response identifies a plausible alternative explanation by noting that highly motivated students may have earned better grades even without attending the workshops.
questions.skill: Identifying a flaw in causal reasoning
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance through Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A school reports that tardiness fell from 8 percent to 6 percent after its start time moved later. Which sentence uses the data appropriately?
choices: After the start time moved later, tardiness fell from 8 percent to 6 percent, so the change certainly caused the entire reduction.
Although tardiness fell after the start time changed, the data prove the later start time had no effect on attendance.
Before the start time changed, tardiness had already fallen to 6 percent, so the later start time was unnecessary.
After the start time moved later, tardiness fell from 8 percent to 6 percent, so the change may have contributed to the reduction.
questions.explanation: The sentence presents the before-and-after change as evidence of a possible contribution rather than proof of sole causation.
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: A speaker claims that a free breakfast program will reduce hunger because each enrolled student receives a meal. Which rebuttal most directly challenges the argument?
choices: Providing meals will not reduce hunger if many students leave them uneaten.
Breakfast menus may need more vegetarian choices than the current plan provides.
Free breakfasts may also give teachers more time to help students settle in.
Students may prefer eating breakfast with friends rather than at school.
questions.explanation: The rebuttal challenges the necessary link between distributing meals and reducing hunger by pointing out that students must actually eat the food.
questions.skill: Identifying the weak link in an argument
questions.topic: Tester 5 of 9: Entry Check, Part 5 of 9

questions.prompt: A master writer is known for reversing repeated grammatical forms to create chiasmus. Which sentence best demonstrates that technique?
choices: The judge asked the witness about the accident, and the witness asked the judge about the rules.
The judge asked the witness about the accident, while the lawyer asked the jury about the rules.
The judge questioned the witness carefully, and the witness answered every question clearly.
After the witness described the accident, the judge asked about the rules governing the testimony.
questions.explanation: The first sentence reverses the judge-witness and witness-judge arrangement, creating the characteristic ABBA structure of chiasmus.
questions.topic: Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A speaker argues that the city should require scooter riders to wear helmets to reduce injuries. A critic says the requirement may discourage some people from riding. Which response best acknowledges the concern while preserving the speaker's argument?
choices: Although some people may choose not to ride scooters if helmets are required, the safety benefits for riders and pedestrians could justify the rule.
If helmet rules discourage some riders, the city should end the program and focus only on making streets safer for cars.
The objection proves that helmet laws are ineffective because worried riders will simply stop using scooters altogether.
Requiring helmets is always the best way to prevent injuries because people dislike the inconvenience of safety rules.
questions.explanation: The response concedes that the requirement may reduce participation while explaining why the potential safety benefits still support the rule.
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: A writer argues that public libraries should stay open on Sundays. Which sentence functions as a concession that strengthens the argument?
choices: Libraries are funded by taxes, so their hours are a public decision.
Some people work on Sundays and rely on libraries for weekend access.
Even though a few branches have staffing problems on Sundays, most libraries could open with adjusted schedules.
Sunday hours would increase electricity costs for every branch.
questions.explanation: This sentence acknowledges a real limitation and then shows why it does not defeat the proposal, which strengthens the argument.
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: A writer describes a city council as determined to improve the streets and reluctant to raise taxes. Which claim about the writer's word choice is best supported?
choices: The two words create a contrast between commitment and hesitation.
The two words show that the council refused to improve the streets.
The two words suggest that the council's actions were widely praised.
The two words indicate that the council had already raised taxes.
questions.explanation: Determined conveys firm commitment while reluctant conveys hesitation, so the pair creates a contrast in the council's actions.
questions.topic: Style Analysis: Imitating the Masters

questions.prompt: A survey found that 62 percent of students in one school preferred online homework, while 55 percent in another school preferred paper homework. Which sentence states the finding with the most appropriate nuance?
choices: Most students in both schools prefer online homework.
Most students in the first school prefer online homework, while a smaller majority in the second prefers paper homework.
Students in the first school prefer online homework more than students in the second school do.
Every student in the first school prefers online homework, and most in the second prefer paper homework.
questions.explanation: This sentence reports both results accurately and preserves the difference between a stronger majority and a narrower one.
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: A library surveys 80 teenage visitors and finds that 58 percent report reading a book for pleasure during their last visit. Which conclusion is fully supported by the survey?
choices: The survey shows that 58 percent of all teenagers read a book for pleasure during their last visit.
Teenagers who visit the library are more likely than nonvisitors to read for pleasure.
Among the surveyed teenage visitors, 58 percent reported reading a book for pleasure during their last visit.
Visiting the library caused 58 percent of the surveyed teenagers to read for pleasure.
questions.explanation: The survey reports only about the sampled teenage visitors, so this conclusion stays within the population and time frame actually measured.
questions.topic: Argument Writing: Rebuttal and Nuance

questions.prompt: The hikers were confused by the directions. They checked the map. Which sentence correctly combines the ideas with a participial phrase that describes the hikers' state?
choices: Confused by the directions, the hikers checked the map.
Checking the map, the hikers were confused by the directions.
The directions, confused by the hikers, were difficult to understand.
Confused by the map, the hikers checked the directions.
questions.explanation: The opening participial phrase describes the hikers' state and correctly modifies the subject of the main clause.
questions.topic: Activity 3 of 9: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The parcel was delayed. The manager wanted to know when. Which sentence correctly combines the ideas with a what-clause?
choices: What the manager wanted to know was when the parcel was delayed.
What the manager wanted to know were when the parcel was delayed.
What the manager wanted to know was the time the parcel was delayed when.
What the manager wanted to know was because the parcel was delayed.
questions.explanation: The what-clause serves as the subject, and the was clause identifies the information the manager wanted.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The rain started. We moved the game indoors. Which sentence uses so to express the cause-and-effect relationship?
choices: The rain started, so we moved the game indoors.
The rain started because we moved the game indoors.
The rain started, although we moved the game indoors.
The rain started, and we moved the game indoors.
questions.explanation: The coordinating conjunction so follows a comma to show that the rain caused the game to be moved indoors.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Nora is a volunteer coach. She runs Saturday drills. Which sentence correctly combines the ideas with an appositive?
choices: Nora, a volunteer coach, runs Saturday drills.
Nora, who is a volunteer coach runs Saturday drills.
Nora a volunteer coach runs Saturday drills.
Nora, a volunteer coach; she runs Saturday drills.
questions.explanation: The appositive a volunteer coach identifies Nora and is correctly enclosed by commas on both sides.
questions.topic: Activity 3 of 9 (quiz/game): Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The final bell rang. The class ended early. Which sentence combines the ideas with an absolute phrase?
choices: The final bell having rung the class ended early.
The final bell had rung, the class ended early.
The final bell having rung, it ended the class early.
The final bell having rung, the class ended early.
questions.explanation: The noun phrase the final bell having rung is an absolute phrase set off by a comma before the main clause.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The northern trail was muddy. The southern trail was dry. Which sentence combines the ideas with a subordinating conjunction that expresses contrast?
choices: The northern trail was muddy, because the southern trail was dry.
The northern trail was muddy, since the southern trail was dry.
The northern trail was muddy, whereas the southern trail was dry.
The northern trail was muddy, if the southern trail was dry.
questions.explanation: Whereas signals a direct contrast between the muddy northern trail and the dry southern trail.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The rehearsal ended early. The actors left the stage. Which sentence correctly combines the two independent clauses with a coordinating conjunction?
choices: The rehearsal ended early, and the actors left the stage.
The rehearsal ended early and, the actors left the stage.
The rehearsal ended early; and the actors left the stage.
The rehearsal ended early, the and actors left the stage.
questions.explanation: A comma before and separates two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The evidence was clear. Everyone understood it. Which sentence correctly combines the ideas with the correlative conjunction so...that?
choices: The evidence was so clear that everyone understood it.
The evidence was such clear that everyone understood it.
The evidence was so clearly that everyone understood it.
The evidence was so clear everyone understood it.
questions.explanation: The correlative pair so...that links the degree of the evidence's clarity with the result that everyone understood it.
questions.topic: Activity 3 of 9 (quiz/game): Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The museum will open early. The train arrives by ten. Which sentence combines the ideas using provided that to express a condition?
choices: If the train arrives by ten, the museum will open early.
The museum will open early provided that the train arrives by ten.
The museum will open early because the train arrives by ten.
The museum will open early when the train arrives by ten.
questions.explanation: Provided that introduces the condition under which the museum will open early.
questions.topic: Activity 3 of 9 (quiz/game): Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Maya designed the poster. It hangs above the bulletin board. Which sentence combines the two ideas using a relative clause?
choices: The poster that Maya designed hangs above the bulletin board.
The poster hangs above the bulletin board that Maya designed.
The poster that Maya designed it hangs above the bulletin board.
The poster that designed by Maya hangs above the bulletin board.
questions.explanation: The relative clause that Maya designed modifies poster and leaves the main clause with the verb hangs.
questions.skill: Combining sentences with a relative clause
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The greenhouse is beside the garden. Seedlings grow there under filtered light. Which sentence correctly combines the ideas with a nonrestrictive relative clause?
choices: The greenhouse, which is beside the garden, is where seedlings grow under filtered light.
The greenhouse is beside the garden, where seedlings grow under filtered light.
The seedlings grow under filtered light, which is the greenhouse beside the garden.
Under the filtered light in the greenhouse, the seedlings grow beside the garden.
questions.explanation: The nonrestrictive clause which is beside the garden adds information about the greenhouse without restricting the meaning of the noun.
questions.topic: Activity 3 of 9: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The evidence was strong. The team changed its plan. Which sentence uses however to show contrast and punctuates it correctly?
choices: The evidence was strong; however, the team changed its plan.
The evidence was strong, however, the team changed its plan.
The evidence was strong however, the team changed its plan.
The evidence was strong, however the team changed its plan.
questions.explanation: The semicolon separates the independent clauses, and the comma after the conjunctive adverb however correctly marks the contrast.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: You can enter with a student ID. You can enter with a guest pass. Which sentence correctly combines the two options with the correlative conjunction either...or?
choices: You can enter with either a student ID or a guest pass.
You can enter with either a student ID and a guest pass.
You can enter with either a student ID nor a guest pass.
You can enter with either a student ID or a guest passes.
questions.explanation: The paired conjunctions either and or correctly offer two alternatives, and the noun phrases a student ID and a guest pass agree in form.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which explanation best identifies why the introductory clause in After the movie ended, we discussed the ending is followed by a comma?
choices: The subordinating conjunction after is always followed by a comma.
The main clause must be separated from its subject because the clause is lengthy.
The introductory dependent clause is separated from the main clause by a comma.
The word ending modifies the movie and needs a comma to mark that relationship.
questions.explanation: A comma conventionally separates an introductory dependent clause from the main clause that follows it.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The technician spoke to the customer. The customer's printer had a paper jam. Which sentence combines the ideas using a possessive relative clause?
choices: The technician spoke to the customer, which printer had a paper jam.
The technician spoke to the customer, whose printer had a paper jam.
The technician spoke to the customer, who printer had a paper jam.
The technician spoke to the customer, whom printer had a paper jam.
questions.explanation: The possessive relative pronoun whose correctly links the customer to the clause describing the customer's printer.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The engineer inspected the bridge. It had several hairline cracks. Which sentence correctly combines the ideas using a relative clause?
choices: The engineer inspected the bridge, which had several hairline cracks.
The engineer inspected the bridge, who had several hairline cracks.
The engineer inspected the bridge, where had several hairline cracks.
The engineer inspected the bridge, whose had several hairline cracks.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun which correctly refers to the bridge and incorporates the information about its cracks.
questions.skill: Combining ideas with a relative clause
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The assistant drafted a checklist. He wanted the new volunteers to be prepared. Which sentence correctly combines the ideas with so that?
choices: The assistant drafted a checklist so that the new volunteers would prepare.
The assistant drafted a checklist so that the new volunteers would be prepared.
The assistant drafted a checklist so that the new volunteers being prepared.
The assistant drafted a checklist so that prepare the new volunteers.
questions.explanation: The so that clause expresses the intended result of drafting the checklist, while would be prepared preserves the volunteers as the passive subject.
questions.skill: Combining an action and its purpose with so that
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The lights went out. The emergency signs appeared immediately. Which sentence presents the signs as appearing right after the lights failed?
choices: As soon as the lights went out, the emergency signs appeared.
Until the lights went out, the emergency signs appeared.
Although the lights went out, the emergency signs appeared.
Unless the lights went out, the emergency signs appeared.
questions.explanation: As soon as introduces a subordinate clause that shows the signs appeared immediately after the lights failed.
questions.skill: Combining sentences with a time conjunction
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The score was excellent. One judge noted a missing citation. Which sentence correctly combines the ideas with the coordinating conjunction however and appropriate punctuation?
choices: The score was excellent; however, one judge noted a missing citation.
The score was excellent, however, one judge noted a missing citation.
The score was excellent: however, one judge noted a missing citation.
The score was excellent however, one judge noted a missing citation.
questions.explanation: A semicolon joins the independent clauses, and however is followed by a comma when it begins the second clause.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which explanation correctly analyzes this complete sentence: When the bus was full, the driver waited for more passengers?
choices: The clause beginning with when is a subordinate clause with a subject and verb, while the main clause also has a subject and verb.
The clause beginning with when is a coordinating conjunction that joins two independent clauses.
The clause beginning with when has no verb, while the main clause supplies the missing subject.
The word when makes both clauses independent, so the sentence needs no main clause.
questions.explanation: The when clause is a complete subordinate clause, and the driver waited for more passengers is the complete main clause.
questions.skill: Explaining the structure of a combined sentence
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The robot sorted the boxes. It also checked each label. Which sentence correctly uses the correlative conjunction not only...but also?
choices: The robot not only sorted the boxes but also checked each label.
The robot either sorted the boxes but also checked each label.
The robot not only sorted the boxes however also checked each label.
The robot neither sorted the boxes but also checked each label.
questions.explanation: Not only and but also form a matched pair that joins two coordinated actions in one sentence.

questions.prompt: The workshop requires three supplies. The supplies are a pen, a notebook, and a pair of scissors. Which sentence correctly introduces the list with a colon?
choices: The workshop requires three supplies: a pen, a notebook, and a pair of scissors.
The workshop requires three supplies, a pen, a notebook, and a pair of scissors.
The workshop requires three supplies; a pen, a notebook, and a pair of scissors.
The workshop requires three supplies because a pen, a notebook, and a pair of scissors.
questions.explanation: The colon appropriately introduces the complete list of supplies after the introductory statement.
questions.skill: Using a colon to introduce a list
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Keep the emergency exit clear. The last student passes through it. Which sentence combines the directions and the event correctly with until?

Keep the emergency exit clear until the last student passing through it.
Keep the emergency exit clear while the last student will pass through it.
Keep the emergency exit clear unless the last student passes through it.
questions.explanation: The clause until the last student passes through it correctly limits how long the emergency exit must remain clear.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: A retired engineer designed the pedestrian bridge. The bridge crosses the river. Which sentence correctly combines the ideas with a relative clause?
choices: A retired engineer who designed the pedestrian bridge crosses the river.
The pedestrian bridge that the retired engineer designed crosses the river.
The retired engineer designed the pedestrian bridge that it crosses the river.
The pedestrian bridge crosses the river that the retired engineer designed.
questions.explanation: The relative clause that the retired engineer designed identifies which pedestrian bridge crosses the river.
questions.skill: Combining sentences with a relative clause
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Ms. Delgado is the new librarian. She has reorganized the reading room. Which sentence combines the two ideas using an appositive?
choices: Ms. Delgado, the new librarian, has reorganized the reading room.
Ms. Delgado, who is the new librarian, has reorganized the reading room.
Ms. Delgado the new librarian has reorganized the reading room.
Ms. Delgado, the new librarian has reorganized the reading room.
questions.explanation: The appositive the new librarian renames Ms. Delgado and is set off by a pair of commas.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The road was closed for repairs. We took a different route. Which sentence makes the road closure the reason for taking another route?
choices: Although the road was closed for repairs, we took a different route.
Since the road was closed for repairs, we took a different route.
Unless the road was closed for repairs, we took a different route.
While the road was closed for repairs, we took a different route.

questions.skill: Combining sentences to express a reason
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The editor cut the final paragraph. She wanted the article to fit on one page. Which sentence combines the ideas by beginning with an infinitive phrase?
choices: To make the article fit on one page, the editor cut the final paragraph.
For making the article fit on one page, the editor cut the final paragraph.
By make the article fit on one page, the editor cut the final paragraph.
The editor cut the final paragraph, to make the article fit on one page.

questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The music played. At the same time, the dancers rehearsed their steps. Which version preserves the simultaneous timing between the music and the rehearsal?

Unless the music played, the dancers rehearsed their steps.
Although the music played, the dancers rehearsed their steps.
While the music played, the dancers rehearsed their steps.

questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Dr. Patel is a marine biologist. She presented her latest research yesterday. Which sentence correctly combines the ideas using an appositive?
choices: Dr. Patel, a marine biologist presented her latest research yesterday.
Dr. Patel, a marine biologist, presented her latest research yesterday.
Dr. Patel a marine biologist, presented her latest research yesterday.
Dr. Patel, marine biologist, presented her latest research yesterday.
questions.explanation: The appositive a marine biologist identifies Dr. Patel and is correctly enclosed by commas.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The bell rang. Everyone left the gym. Which explanation best identifies why the semicolon correctly joins these two independent clauses?
choices: The two independent clauses are closely related, so a semicolon joins them without creating a comma splice.
The second clause is dependent on the first, so a semicolon completes the shared subject and verb.
The two clauses have different subjects, so a semicolon can replace the missing verb in the second clause.
The first clause contains a prepositional phrase, so a semicolon separates it from the main clause.
questions.explanation: The semicolon marks the boundary between two closely related independent clauses without incorrectly joining them with only a comma.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Suppose the school extends the deadline. Students will have more time to revise. Which sentence combines the ideas as an unreal condition using the second conditional?
choices: If the school extends the deadline, students will have more time to revise.
If the school extended the deadline, students would have more time to revise.
If the school would extend the deadline, students will have more time to revise.
If the school had extended the deadline, students would have had more time to revise.
questions.explanation: The second conditional uses a past-tense if-clause and would followed by a base verb to frame the deadline extension as hypothetical.
questions.skill: Combining sentences with the second conditional
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The alarm sounded. The students left because of the alarm. Which sentence combines the ideas with a that-clause introduced by the reason?
choices: The reason the alarm sounded was that the students left the building.
The reason the students left the building was because the alarm sounded.
The reason the students left the building was that the alarm sounded.
The reason of the students left the building was that the alarm sounded.
questions.explanation: The construction the reason the students left the building was that the alarm sounded presents the alarm as the reason for the students' departure.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The curator unlocked the gallery at noon. The visitors entered at 12:05. Which sentence correctly combines the ideas with the subordinating conjunction after?
choices: After the curator unlocked the gallery at noon, the visitors entered at 12:05.
After the visitors entered at 12:05, the curator unlocked the gallery at noon.
Although the curator unlocked the gallery at noon, the visitors entered at 12:05.
Because the curator unlocked the gallery at noon, the visitors entered at 12:05.
questions.explanation: The introductory clause beginning with after correctly shows that the gallery was unlocked before the visitors entered.
questions.skill: Combining ideas with a subordinating conjunction
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The coach praised the violinist. The violinist had learned the solo. Which sentence correctly combines the ideas with a relative clause?
choices: The coach praised the violinist who had learned the solo.
The coach praised the violinist whom had learned the solo.
The coach praised the violinist which had learned the solo.
The coach praised the violinist whose had learned the solo.
questions.explanation: Who serves as the subject of had learned within the relative clause that identifies the violinist the coach praised.

questions.prompt: The museum has one student discount. Visitors must show their IDs. Which sentence correctly combines the ideas with a colon?

The museum has one student discount; visitors must show their IDs.
The museum has one student discount, visitors must show their IDs.
The museum has one student discount visitors must show their IDs.
questions.explanation: The colon correctly introduces the specific condition that visitors must show their IDs to receive the student discount.
