meta.subject: English
meta.topic: Activity 1 of 9 (quiz/game): Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft
meta.title: Notice It: Advanced Syntax in the Model Text

questions.prompt: Which model sentence contains a conditional clause?
choices: If the museum opens by noon, visitors will enter through the east gate.
Although the museum opens by noon, visitors will enter through the east gate.
While the museum opens by noon, visitors will enter through the east gate.
Because the museum opens by noon, visitors will enter through the east gate.
questions.explanation: The clause if the museum opens by noon is a conditional clause that states a condition for visitors entering through the east gate.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence contains a reduced relative clause modifying report?
choices: The report submitted by the committee won approval.
The report was submitted by the committee before approval.
The committee submitted the report and won approval.
The committee submitted the report before it won approval.
questions.explanation: In the correct sentence, submitted by the committee is a reduced relative clause that modifies report.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: In the model sentence Although the rehearsal had started, the actors changed the set, which part is the independent clause?
choices: although the rehearsal had started
the actors changed the set
that they had prepared earlier
who had prepared the set earlier
questions.explanation: The actors changed the set is the independent clause because it contains a subject and a finite verb and can stand alone.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a complex sentence?
choices: Because the power failed, the elevator stopped between floors.
The elevator stopped between floors, and the passengers became concerned.
The elevator stopped between floors, the passengers became concerned, and the operator spoke calmly.
The elevator stopped between floors and remained still.
questions.explanation: Because the power failed is a dependent clause, while the elevator stopped between floors is the independent clause.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence correctly joins two independent clauses with a semicolon?
choices: The storm ended; sunlight crossed the field.
The storm ended, sunlight crossed the field.
The storm ended and sunlight crossed the field.
Because the storm ended, sunlight crossed the field.
questions.explanation: A semicolon can join two closely related independent clauses, as it does between ended and sunlight.
questions.skill: Identify a semicolon joining independent clauses
questions.topic: Activity 1 of 9 (quiz/game): Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence uses causative have with a past participle?
choices: The family had the old fence rebuilt before spring.
The family rebuilt the old fence before spring.
The family had rebuilt the old fence before spring.
The family was rebuilding the old fence before spring.
questions.explanation: The causative construction had the old fence rebuilt presents the family as arranging for the fence to be rebuilt.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence uses a gerund phrase as its subject?
choices: Winning the debate strengthened Maya's confidence.
The coach praised Priya after completing the relay.
The judge recommended practicing before the recital.
The coach praised Priya's completing the relay.
questions.explanation: The gerund phrase Winning the debate functions as the complete subject of the sentence.
questions.skill: Identify a gerund phrase used as a subject
questions.topic: Activity 1 of 9 (quiz/game): Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence is a rhetorical question?
choices: Who would trade a steady rhythm for a flawless mistake?
The steady rhythm sounded better than the flawless mistake.
What a steady rhythm sounded like in the rehearsal room!
Listen for the steady rhythm inside every rehearsal.
questions.explanation: The sentence poses a question that emphasizes the value of a steady rhythm without expecting a factual response.
questions.skill: Identifying rhetorical questions in a model sentence
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence opens with a fronted prepositional phrase?
choices: Leaves skittered across the courtyard in the wind.
Skittering across the courtyard, the leaves stirred the air.
Across the courtyard, leaves skittered in the wind.
That the leaves crossed the courtyard surprised the gardener.
questions.explanation: The prepositional phrase Across the courtyard appears at the beginning of the sentence before its subject and verb.
questions.skill: Identifying fronted prepositional phrases in a model sentence
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence is cumulative, building through a series of coordinated actions?
choices: The child opened the box after the lid was lifted.
The child opened the box, and a glowing marble appeared inside.
Opening the box, the child found a glowing marble inside.
The child opened the box, lifted the lid, and found a glowing marble.
questions.explanation: This cumulative sentence begins with a main clause and then adds a series of coordinated actions.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence uses an infinitive phrase as a subject complement?
choices: The challenge was to solve the final problem before sunset.
To solve the final problem before sunset was the challenge.
The challenge of solving the final problem was before sunset.
The challenge was that the team would solve the final problem.
questions.explanation: The infinitive phrase to solve the final problem before sunset functions as the subject complement of was.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a compound sentence that uses the coordinating conjunction but?
choices: The librarian sorted the books, but the students chose their favorites.
The librarian sorted the books because the students chose their favorites.
The librarian sorted the books while the students chose their favorites.
The librarian sorted the books, and the students chose their favorites.
questions.explanation: The sentence is a compound sentence because two independent clauses are joined by the coordinating conjunction but.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence uses a noun clause as its subject?
choices: What the team accomplished earned praise.
The team accomplished what the coach had planned.
When the team returns, practice will continue.
The coach knew what the team had accomplished.
questions.explanation: The noun clause What the team accomplished functions as the complete subject of the sentence.
questions.skill: Identify a noun clause used as a subject
questions.topic: Activity 1 of 9 (quiz/game): Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence uses an infinitive phrase as its subject?
choices: Preserving the old theater was the committee's first priority.
The committee's first priority was to preserve the old theater.
To preserve the old theater was the committee's first priority.
Whether to preserve the old theater was the committee's first priority.
questions.explanation: The infinitive phrase to preserve the old theater functions as the subject of the sentence.
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a colon to introduce an explanation?
choices: The evidence was clear: the footprints matched the missing shoe.
The evidence was clear, the footprints matched the missing shoe.
The evidence was clear; the footprints matched the missing shoe.
The evidence was clear the footprints matched the missing shoe.
questions.explanation: The colon after clear properly introduces an explanation expressed as a complete independent clause.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence presents three actions in grammatically parallel form?
choices: The essay required researching, drafting, and revising.
The essay required researching, drafting, and the revision.
The essay required to research, drafting, and revising.
The essay required research, drafted, and revising.
questions.explanation: The three gerunds researching, drafting, and revising are grammatically parallel and complete the required actions.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains a subordinate clause expressing time?
choices: The crew repaired the roof, and the neighbors offered help.
The crew, exhausted by the storm, repaired the roof.
After the storm passed, the crew repaired the roof.
The crew repaired the roof because the storm had passed.
questions.explanation: The clause after the storm passed tells when the crew repaired the roof, so it expresses time.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence is balanced, with two parallel independent clauses?
choices: The gardener watered the roses, and the neighbor trimmed the hedges.
The gardener watered the roses before the neighbor trimmed the hedges.
After watering the roses, the gardener noticed the neighbor trimming the hedges.
The gardener, who found the roses dry, fetched the hose.
questions.explanation: This sentence is balanced because its two independent clauses have parallel subject-verb-object structures.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence correctly uses a colon to introduce a list?
choices: The revised schedule includes three stops: a bakery, a library, and a park.
The revised schedule includes three stops, a bakery, a library, and a park.
The revised schedule includes three stops—a bakery, a library, and a park.
The revised schedule includes three stops (a bakery, a library, and a park).
questions.explanation: The colon introduces the list of three stops, which is its standard punctuation use.
questions.skill: Use a colon correctly before a list
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence uses a parallel pair of adverbs to describe how the judge questioned the witness?
choices: The judge questioned the witness calmly and precisely.
The judge questioned the witness calmly and in a precise manner.
The judge calmly questioned the witness with precision.
The judge questioned the witness with calmness and with precision.
questions.explanation: The adverbs calmly and precisely form a parallel pair describing the verb questioned.
questions.skill: Maintain parallel structure in a sentence
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence contains a nonrestrictive relative clause?
choices: The violinist who had won the competition opened the concert.
The violinist, who had won the competition, opened the concert.
The violinist who opened the concert had won the competition.
The violinist had won the competition before opening the concert.
questions.explanation: The clause who had won the competition is nonrestrictive because commas set it off as additional information about the violinist.
questions.topic: Activity 1 of 9 (quiz/game): Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses anacoluthon, breaking from an expected grammatical pattern?
choices: The guide introduced the trail, described the landmarks, and then the hikers set off.
The guide introduced the trail, described the landmarks, and warned the hikers.
After the guide described the landmarks, the hikers set off.
The guide introduced the trail because the hikers wanted a clear route.
questions.explanation: The construction shifts from the guide as the subject to the hikers as a new subject, creating an abrupt break in syntactic parallelism.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence has a compound predicate?
choices: The technician calibrated the instrument and replaced the faulty cable.
The technician calibrated the instrument, and the assistant replaced the faulty cable.
The technician calibrated the instrument after the assistant replaced the faulty cable.
The technician calibrated the instrument, although the assistant replaced the faulty cable.
questions.explanation: The compound predicate consists of calibrated the instrument and replaced the faulty cable, which share the subject The technician.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence opens with a participial phrase that expresses cause?
choices: When the strong wind shook the canvas tent, it collapsed near the ridge.
Shaken by the strong wind, the canvas tent collapsed near the ridge.
After the canvas tent collapsed near the ridge, the strong wind shook it.
Because the canvas tent collapsed near the ridge, the strong wind shook it.
questions.explanation: The opening participial phrase Shaken by the strong wind identifies the cause of the tent's collapse.
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence contains an absolute phrase?
choices: Maya turned the page with trembling hands.
Her hands trembling, Maya turned the page.
Maya, turning the page, noticed a folded note.
After her hands began trembling, Maya turned the page.
questions.explanation: Her hands trembling is an absolute phrase because its implied subject differs from the main subject, Maya.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses antithesis to contrast two ideas in parallel structure?
choices: Some athletes train for strength; others train for speed.
The referee checked the score, and the audience began to cheer.
After the storm passed, sunlight brightened the field.
The old bridge was narrow but sturdy.
questions.explanation: The sentence contrasts two ideas in parallel clauses beginning with Some athletes and others, which makes it an example of antithesis.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence uses a deliberate sentence fragment to create emphasis?
choices: Across the field, silence fell.
Silence fell across the field.
Across the field, silence.
The field was filled with silence.
questions.explanation: The model sentence is a deliberate fragment because it has no finite verb and uses the isolated image for emphasis.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence uses paired dashes to set off an interruption?
choices: The coach—one of the few who never missed practice—kept the team focused.
The coach, one of the few who never missed practice, kept the team focused.
The coach (one of the few who never missed practice) kept the team focused.
The coach: one of the few who never missed practice, kept the team focused.
questions.explanation: The paired dashes set off the interruption one of the few who never missed practice from the rest of the sentence.
questions.skill: Use paired dashes to frame an interruption
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly places a comma before a coordinating conjunction joining two independent clauses?
choices: The package was lightweight, yet it contained three books.
The package was lightweight yet it contained three books.
The package was lightweight; and it contained three books.
The package was lightweight; it contained three books.
questions.explanation: A comma correctly separates the independent clause The package was lightweight from the independent clause it contained three books before the coordinating conjunction yet.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence correctly agrees with the singular indefinite pronoun each?
choices: Each of the hikers carries a map.
Each of the hikers carry a map.
Each of the hikers are carrying a map.
Each of the hikers have a map.
questions.explanation: The singular subject each agrees with the singular verb carries even though the prepositional phrase of the hikers intervenes.
questions.skill: Maintain subject-verb agreement across an intervening phrase
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence is compound-complex, combining dependent and independent clauses?
choices: Although rain drummed against the windows, the hikers pressed on.
Although rain drummed against the windows, the hikers pressed on, and their guide checked the map.
The hikers pressed on, and their guide checked the map.
The hikers pressed on while their guide checked the map under the drumming rain.
questions.explanation: This sentence contains one dependent clause and two independent clauses.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence is periodic, placing its main clause after an introductory dependent clause?
choices: The orchestra finished the final note, and silence filled the theater.
When the orchestra finished the final note, silence filled the theater.
The orchestra finished the final note before silence filled the theater.
Finishing the final note, the orchestra received enthusiastic applause.
questions.explanation: Its introductory dependent clause delays the main clause until the end of the sentence.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence uses inversion to create emphasis?
choices: The apprentice crept into the quiet workshop.
While the workshop was quiet, the apprentice crept inside.
Into the quiet workshop crept the apprentice.
Quietly the apprentice crept into the workshop.
questions.explanation: The sentence moves the subject, the apprentice, after the verb and places the prepositional phrase first to create emphasis.
questions.skill: Identifying inversion in a model sentence
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence contains a participial phrase modifying the direct object?
choices: The curator examined the photograph hanging above the desk.
The curator, examining the photograph, wrote the report.
The curator examined the photograph that hung above the desk.
The curator examined the photograph and wrote the report.
questions.explanation: The participial phrase hanging above the desk modifies the direct object photograph.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence contains a noun clause serving as the object of a preposition?
choices: The final decision depends on the team's ability to finish on time.
The final decision depends on whether the team can finish on time.
The final decision depends on the team, which can finish on time.
The final decision depends on the possibility of an on-time finish.
questions.explanation: Whether the team can finish on time is a noun clause serving as the object of the preposition on.
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence uses the correlative pair not only...but also with parallel verbs?
choices: The guide either described the route or warned us about the current.
The guide neither described the route nor warned us about the current.
The guide not only described the route but also warned us about the current.
The guide both described the route and warned us about the current.
questions.explanation: The sentence correctly uses not only...but also to coordinate two parallel verbs, described and warned.
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence begins with a participial phrase that modifies the subject?
choices: To reach the gate, Lena carried a red umbrella.
Walking toward the gate, Lena carried a red umbrella.
Lena, the captain of the team, carried a red umbrella.
Because the gate was locked, Lena carried a red umbrella.
questions.explanation: The introductory phrase Walking toward the gate is a participial phrase that modifies Lena.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which option uses anadiplosis by repeating the final word of one sentence at the beginning of the next?
choices: The bell rang in the hall. The hall echoed with the final note.
The bell rang. Students entered the quiet hallway.
The bell rang, and students entered the quiet hallway.
When the bell rang, students entered the quiet hallway.
questions.explanation: The second sentence begins with hall, the final word of the preceding sentence, creating the pattern called anadiplosis.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence uses as...as to make a comparison?
choices: This trail is as steep as the quarry road.
This trail appears steeper than the quarry road.
This trail and the quarry road are equally steep.
The quarry road's steepness resembles that of this trail.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses the paired correlative construction as...as to compare the steepness of the trail and the quarry road.
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses either and or to connect two parallel verb phrases?
choices: The visitors either completed the form at the desk or called the office.
The visitors either completed the form at the desk nor called the office.
The visitors completed the form at the desk and either called the office.
The visitors neither completed the form at the desk nor called the office.
questions.explanation: Either and or connect the parallel verb phrases completed and called and present them as alternatives.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence contains an appositive phrase?
choices: The coach, whom the students trusted, adjusted the score.
The coach, a former violinist, adjusted the score.
The coach, after a long rehearsal, adjusted the score.
The violinist coached the team and adjusted the score.
questions.explanation: The phrase a former violinist is an appositive because it renames the coach with additional information.
questions.skill: Identifying an appositive phrase in a model sentence
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains a noun clause serving as the direct object of a verb?
choices: The coach explained that the final round had been postponed.
The coach explained because the final round had been postponed.
The coach's explanation concerned the postponement of the final round.
The coach explained the postponement after the judges arrived.
questions.explanation: The noun clause that the final round had been postponed functions as the direct object of explained.
questions.skill: Identify a noun clause used as a direct object
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: In the model sentence The hikers followed the narrow passage through the forest, what is the object of the preposition through?
choices: the hikers
the narrow passage
the passage
the forest
questions.explanation: The preposition through takes the object the forest, which names the area crossed by the hikers.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence contains a restrictive relative clause modifying manuscript?
choices: The manuscript lay beneath the editor's unfinished notes.
The manuscript, which the editor praised, was bound in blue.
The manuscript was bound in blue after the editor praised it.
The manuscript that the editor praised was bound in blue.
questions.explanation: The clause that the editor praised restricts the meaning of the noun manuscript to a particular one.
questions.skill: Identifying restrictive relative clauses in a model sentence
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence uses an emphatic cleft to focus on the person performing the action?
choices: It was the pilot who guided the plane safely.
The pilot guided the plane safely during the storm.
It was the plane that the pilot safely guided.
The pilot, who guided the plane safely, received an award.
questions.explanation: The emphatic cleft It was the pilot who guided the plane safely places emphasis on the person who performed the action.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence uses there as an existential expletive?
choices: There are three reasons for changing the schedule.
The three reasons are for changing the schedule.
The committee cited three reasons for changing the schedule.
Three reasons for changing the schedule are in the meeting notes.
questions.explanation: The word there introduces the existence of three reasons without serving as the subject of the sentence.
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Identify the sentence that uses parataxis, placing independent clauses side by side without a conjunction.
choices: The lights dimmed. The audience opened the programs.
The lights dimmed, and the audience opened the programs.
When the lights dimmed, the audience opened the programs.
The lights dimmed as the audience opened the programs.
questions.explanation: The two complete sentences place independent clauses side by side without a conjunction, illustrating parataxis.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence correctly uses neither...nor to coordinate two subjects?
choices: Neither the rain nor the strong wind stopped the cyclists.
Either the rain or the strong wind stopped the cyclists.
The rain weakened, but the strong wind still stopped the cyclists.
Because the rain and wind were weak, the cyclists continued.
questions.explanation: Neither...nor joins the subjects rain and strong wind in a single clause with the finite verb stopped.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains a dangling participial modifier?
choices: Hoping for a reply, the letter was placed in the drawer.
Looking both ways, Lena crossed the busy street.
Shaken by the wind, the sign swung repeatedly.
Given the correct time, the coach began the race.
questions.explanation: The opening participial phrase logically modifies the letter rather than the person who placed it in the drawer.
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which model sentence contains an object complement?
choices: The judges called the performance unforgettable.
The judges handed the captain the trophy.
The judges were impressed by the performance.
The judges left the theater before the award.
questions.explanation: The adjective unforgettable is an object complement because it describes the direct object performance.
questions.topic: Activity 1 of 9 (quiz/game): Notice It in a Model Text - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

feedback.correct: Sharp eye — that pattern is exactly what the model text wanted you to notice.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Re-read the sentence and ask where the main clause lands.
feedback.win: Wall cleared! You can now spot periodic, cumulative, and balanced sentences on sight.
feedback.lose: The wall holds this time. Look for where the main clause sits before the next serve.

meta.subject: English
meta.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9
meta.title: Entry Check, Part 9: Digital and Multimodal Composition through College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: Which combination of choices best presents data accessibly in a college report that must work on slow connections and with assistive technologies?
choices: Provide a text summary and data table for every chart, keep labels legible, and do not rely on color alone.
Provide a detailed alt-text field for every chart, but replace the data table with links that may require an internet connection.
Present the data as color-coded images, add a paragraph describing the main trend, and omit labels for individual values.
Use a text table for the data and describe each chart's title, but convey category distinctions only through color.
questions.explanation: This approach provides text-based equivalents and clear labels without making color perception or network access necessary for understanding the data.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: An essay argues that public service announcements about water safety can improve students' habits. A study finds that students who saw a water-safety announcement were more likely to report changing a drinking routine than students who did not see one. Which sentence uses the study accurately and advances the argument?
choices: Because every student who saw the water-safety announcement changed a drinking routine, the announcement was more effective than any health campaign.
Students who saw a water-safety announcement were more likely to report changing a drinking routine, providing evidence that such announcements can influence habits.
Students who did not see the announcement avoided changing their routines, proving that announcements reduce healthy behavior.
The announcement changed students' routines, so schools should require every student to view it before classes.
questions.explanation: This sentence accurately reports the relationship found in the study and uses cautious language that supports the argument without claiming proof of universal causation.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: An essay asks students to evaluate how digital tools can support or hinder their preparation for college. Which is the strongest thesis for the essay?
choices: Because digital tools expand access to research and feedback while requiring deliberate use, their value in college preparation depends on how students apply them.
Digital tools are important in college preparation because they are widely available to students.
This essay will examine digital tools by discussing research databases, video lectures, and learning applications.
Digital tools have changed education, but only one of those changes directly affects college preparation.
questions.explanation: This thesis presents a qualified, arguable position that addresses both the benefits and limitations of digital tools.
questions.topic: College-Level Writing: Thesis Development

questions.prompt: A survey found that students who used a note-taking app revised their drafts more often, although app use was voluntary and motivation also affected revision frequency. Which conclusion is warranted?
choices: Note-taking app use was associated with more revisions, but the survey does not establish causation.
Note-taking apps caused more revisions because frequent app users revised their drafts more often.
Students should avoid note-taking apps because motivation affects how often they revise.
Motivation explains all differences in revision frequency because app use had no relationship with it.
questions.explanation: The survey supports an association between app use and revision frequency but cannot show that one factor caused the other.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: A college essay argues that selective colleges should replace a legacy admissions advantage with need-based aid. Which sentence most directly establishes the writer's credibility through ethos?
choices: Imagine an applicant whose years of effort are overlooked because her parents never attended an elite school.
Research from several universities shows that need-based grants improve completion rates among low-income students.
A selective college that values fairness should not reserve advantages for families who need no help.
As a former admissions officer who reviewed thousands of files, I can explain how small advantages in legacy status compound over time.
questions.explanation: The writer's specific professional experience establishes relevant authority, which is the basis of ethos.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 9: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: An online article claims that a university's six-year graduation rate rose after a new course requirement took effect. Which source would provide the strongest verification of both the change and its timing?
choices: Official university reports that give graduation rates for named cohorts and identify when the requirement took effect.
A student association survey asking graduates whether the requirement improved their experience.
A news editorial that describes the requirement as successful without presenting outcome data.
A cached copy of the course webpage that lists the requirement's topics and credit hours.
questions.explanation: Official reports can connect dated graduation data with the policy timeline, while the other sources do not establish the reported change in outcomes.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: A student is making a line chart of monthly public-library visits from 2020 to 2024, but no values were collected for 2022. Which treatment is most accurate?
choices: Leave a labeled gap at 2022 and break the line between the 2021 and 2023 points.
Connect 2021 directly to 2023 with a solid line so the monthly trend appears continuous.
Enter zero for every missing month in 2022 and include those zeros in the average.
Compress the horizontal spacing so that 2021 and 2023 appear adjacent while keeping 2022 off the axis.
questions.explanation: A labeled gap accurately distinguishes uncollected data from observed values and prevents the chart from implying a measured trend across 2022.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 9: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: In a reflective college-application essay, a teacher wrote See what you can do with it beside a student's weak first draft. Which sentence best turns the incident into meaningful reflection by showing a changed understanding and its significance?
choices: My teacher wrote See what you can do with it beside my first draft in blue ink.
I felt nervous when I read my teacher's comment beside the first draft I had submitted.
That comment made me see revision as a way to solve problems rather than as a test of fixed ability, which changed how I approached later work.
A first draft is usually rough, and a teacher can leave encouraging remarks on it.
questions.explanation: The sentence connects the teacher's comment to a new way of understanding revision and explains how that change affected the student's later work.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 9: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: Which set of three gerund phrases can serve as parallel steps in a process guide?
choices: Downloading the dataset, cleaning the records, and exporting a summary
To download the dataset, cleaning the records, and to export a summary
Downloading the dataset, records being cleaned, and exporting a summary
The dataset downloaded, records cleaned, and a summary exported
questions.explanation: Each phrase begins with a gerund and expresses one action in the same grammatical form, creating parallel structure.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: A school wants to determine whether a five-minute writing warm-up improves students' performance on timed essays. Which study design would provide the strongest causal evidence?
choices: Randomly assign students to a five-minute writing warm-up or an equal period of silent reading, then have blinded raters score their timed essays.
Compare scores from students who volunteer for the warm-up with scores from students who skip it.
Survey students after a timed essay about whether the writing warm-up felt useful.
Review essays from warm-up sessions to determine whether their introductions are longer.
questions.explanation: Random assignment limits preexisting differences between groups, while blinded scoring makes the comparison more objective.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: A student uses an AI tool to suggest essay topics, then selects one and develops an original argument with credible research. Which disclosure is most accurate?
choices: The student used AI only to correct spelling because no ideas came from the tool.
The student used AI to write the complete essay and changed a few details afterward.
The student wrote the essay independently and did not use AI at all.
The student used AI to brainstorm topics, then independently evaluated the suggestions and developed the final argument.
questions.explanation: This disclosure accurately identifies the tool's limited role while acknowledging the student's own research, judgment, and writing.
questions.topic: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: A student needs reliable, current evidence about how much sleep teenagers get. Which source should the student consult first?
choices: A government health report that explains its survey methods and links to the data
A health blog post that summarizes one sleep study without naming its methods
A newspaper article that reports survey findings but gives no source details
An encyclopedia entry that defines adolescent sleep but predates recent data
questions.explanation: The government report is the strongest starting point because it identifies its methods, supports its findings with data, and is more suitable for current research than the other sources.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: A historian wants to verify the exact wording a president used in a 1943 address. Which source is most appropriate?
choices: A digitized stenographic transcript of the address prepared at the time
A modern opinion article interpreting the address's historical significance
A textbook paragraph summarizing the address's main argument
A documentary reenactment presenting the address several decades later
questions.explanation: A contemporaneous stenographic transcript is a primary source that most directly preserves the president's original wording.
questions.topic: Digital and Multimodal Composition: Primary Source Evaluation

questions.prompt: A student creates an infographic summarizing the causes and effects of urban heat islands. Which design choice best supports accurate interpretation and accessibility?
choices: Use bright colors without labels so the most important ideas attract attention first.
Place the full explanation in speaker notes while leaving the infographic mostly decorative.
Use icons for every statistic without stating the measurements they represent.
Use a labeled diagram that distinguishes measured data from causal explanations and states the source below it.
questions.explanation: The labeled diagram, clear distinction between data and explanation, and source note make the infographic interpretable without relying on color or hidden audio.
questions.topic: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: A student wants to revise this sentence without changing its meaning: Although the final chart showed a steady rise, its caption explained that the increase applied only to online courses. Which revision replaces the ambiguous pronoun with a possessive noun phrase?
choices: Although the final chart showed a steady rise, its authors explained that the increase applied only to online courses.
Although the final chart showed a steady rise, the chart's data explained that the increase applied only to online courses.
Although the final chart showed a steady rise, the image's title explained that the increase applied only to online courses.
Although the final chart showed a steady rise, the chart's caption explained that the increase applied only to online courses.
questions.explanation: The phrase the chart's caption clearly identifies what explained the limitation and preserves the original meaning.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: A school randomly assigns half of its writing students to a weekly one-to-one conference and half to a conference every three weeks. At the end of the term, the weekly group revised more successfully on average. Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: The weekly-conference group showed better average revision performance than the every-three-weeks group in this study.
Weekly conferences improve revision performance for every student at the school.
The results prove that motivation was the only factor that affected students' revision performance.
Conferences every three weeks provide no benefit because the weekly group performed better on average.
questions.explanation: The conclusion states the observed group difference without extending the study's results beyond its participants or conditions.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: A video essay combines a graph showing changes over time with a photograph illustrating one event. Which design choice best distinguishes the graph's data from the photograph's illustrative role?
choices: Label the graph's axes, years, and source, and caption the photograph as an illustration of one event rather than evidence of the overall trend.
Give the graph and photograph matching colors so viewers perceive them as parts of the same dataset.
Place the photograph beside the graph without a caption so it provides independent visual confirmation.
Scale the photograph to the graph's vertical axis so its height can be compared with each data point.
questions.explanation: Clear labels identify the graph as measured data, while the photograph's caption prevents one example from being mistaken for evidence of the overall trend.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: A college essay quotes a state senator from a livestream. Which citation gives readers enough information to find the statement and assess its context?
choices: The senator's surname, the word speech, the platform name, and a link to the channel's home page.
The platform name, the video's follower count, the quoted passage, and the video's upload date.
The senator's full name, the campaign issue, the campaign website, and the quoted passage.
The senator's surname, the event date, the audience size, and the general name of the platform.
questions.explanation: A surname, program title, and channel link can help readers locate the recording, while the upload date supports assessment of when the statement was made.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: A student wants to introduce and emphasize three advantages of a proposal in a college essay. Which sentence uses a colon correctly to introduce the list?
choices: The proposal costs less, it reaches more students, and it requires no new staff.
The proposal: it costs less, it reaches more students, and it requires no new staff.
The proposal costs less: it reaches more students, and it requires no new staff.
The proposal has three advantages: it costs less, it reaches more students, and it requires no new staff.
questions.explanation: The colon follows a complete introductory phrase and correctly introduces three parallel clauses that specify the proposal's advantages.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: A researcher finds a viral statistic claiming that students spend more time on screens than sleeping. Which next step best verifies the claim?
choices: Search for a government or research report that identifies its data source, sample, and collection date.
Open several social media posts and count how many repeat the same statistic.
Ask classmates whether they believe the statistic reflects their own screen use.
Repost the statistic with a warning while waiting for a more reliable source.
questions.explanation: A government or research report that explains its data source, sample, and collection date allows the researcher to judge whether the viral statistic is supported and current.
questions.topic: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: A student creates an interactive timeline whose events can be opened for details. Which feature best allows a keyboard user to access every event and understand whether it is open or closed?
choices: Each event is reachable only by clicking with a pointer, while its details appear in a hover tooltip.
The timeline advances automatically every five seconds, and each event closes after a fixed display time.
Each event is reachable in a logical keyboard-focus order, can be opened with Enter or Space, and exposes its state to assistive technology.
Each event appears as a separate file that users must download and open in a desktop spreadsheet.
questions.explanation: Logical keyboard focus, keyboard-operable controls, and an exposed state make the timeline's events accessible without relying on pointer gestures.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: A paragraph must compare a historian's account of a protest with a later documentary about official responses. Which sentence best integrates both sources and explains the significance of their differences?
choices: Both sources describe the protest, but only the documentary identifies a date and location.
The protest occurred before the documentary was created, and the historian's account is also about that event.
Both accounts describe the protest, but the historian focuses on crowd emotions while the documentary emphasizes official decisions, revealing different priorities.
The historian explains what participants felt, while the documentary records what officials decided.
questions.explanation: The sentence integrates details from both sources and explains how their different emphases affect the historian's interpretation.
questions.topic: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: Which statement most effectively frames a focused, arguable thesis about preparing for college-level writing?
choices: Students develop stronger college writing by analyzing evidence, revising drafts, and responding to feedback.
College-level writing includes reading, researching, drafting, and revising in many assignments.
High school students can begin preparing for college writing by completing assignments in English classes.
College writing courses are usually more difficult than the English courses students take in high school.
questions.explanation: The thesis presents a specific, arguable position about how students develop college-level writing skills.
questions.topic: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: The sentence After completing the online course, the certificate appeared in Maya's inbox contains a dangling modifier. Which revision fixes the modifier while preserving the intended meaning?
choices: After completing the online course, Maya received her certificate in her inbox.
After completing the online course, the certificate arrived in Maya's inbox.
Completing the online course, the certificate was emailed to Maya.
After the online course being completed, Maya received her certificate in her inbox.
questions.explanation: The revised sentence makes Maya the subject of completing the course, so the introductory modifier correctly describes her action.
questions.topic: Advanced Grammar Review: Modifier Placement

questions.prompt: A student includes one brief quotation from a copyrighted article to analyze how its wording frames a claim. Which plan best follows ethical digital citation practice?
choices: Use only the portion needed for analysis, cite it, and explain how the wording supports the student's point.
Use a longer section for context, cite it, and replace original analysis with a summary.
Use only the portion needed for analysis, paraphrase it closely, and omit attribution.
Use a brief portion for analysis, cite it, and publish it as the main focus without commentary.
questions.explanation: This plan limits the use to what analysis requires, provides attribution, and adds original commentary rather than substituting the source for the student's work.
questions.topic: Digital and Multimodal Composition: Copyright and Fair Use

questions.prompt: A student wants to determine whether an online archive page quoted in a 2012 article has since been edited. Which action provides the strongest evidence?
choices: Retrieve archived versions and compare their wording, dates, and metadata.
Ask the current page administrator whether an earlier version exists.
Compare the article with the current page and infer that every difference is an edit.
Download the current page and count how often its key terms appear.
questions.explanation: Archived versions can establish how the page changed over time, while dates and metadata help distinguish genuine revisions from differences in presentation.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: Ruiz has two works, one from 2022 and one from 2024, and both are cited in the same sentence. Which parenthetical citation follows APA 7 style?
questions.explanation: APA style places the author's name before multiple years and separates the years with commas in chronological order.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 9: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: A student is comparing two infographics about digital reading. One begins in 2010 and includes all readers, while the other begins in 2015 and includes only registered subscribers. Which response best evaluates the comparison?
choices: Combine both series into one total because each one displays digital reading activity over time.
Compare only the years that appear in both series, after noting that the populations and start dates differ.
Treat the longer series as more accurate because it includes more years of data.
Compare the first data points in the two series because they represent the same group of readers.
questions.explanation: Comparing shared years while identifying differences in populations and dates prevents the student from treating unlike measures as directly equivalent.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: A student uses a generative AI tool to suggest counterarguments for a debate, then writes final paragraphs without checking the suggestions. Which action best follows responsible academic practice?
choices: Compare each suggestion with credible sources and rewrite or remove claims that cannot be supported.
Submit the generated counterarguments because they make the debate sound more convincing.
Keep the suggestions unchanged but replace the names of several cited authors.
Disclose only the portions that exactly match sentences in the tool's output.
questions.explanation: Comparing AI-generated claims with credible sources and revising unsupported material helps the student retain accuracy and academic responsibility.
questions.topic: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: A student is checking whether the paragraphs in a college essay work together logically. Which reverse-outline notes provide the strongest diagnostic?
choices: List every citation, quotation, and image in the order it appears in the essay.
Summarize each paragraph's main claim, then label how it advances, supports, or qualifies the thesis.
Copy the essay's first sentence, last sentence, and transition words into a separate list.
Count the words, sources, and paragraphs devoted to each broad topic.
questions.explanation: A reverse outline is most useful when it identifies each paragraph's claim and function so the student can evaluate the argument's logical progression.
questions.topic: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: A student is revising a class presentation for readability and accessibility. Which change best follows both principles?
choices: Replace dense paragraphs with brief bullet points, add relevant high-contrast visuals, and include alt text.
Keep full paragraphs on each slide, but add a decorative image and brighter text for emphasis.
Use two visually similar fonts, center all text, and describe the slides aloud during the presentation.
Add unlabeled charts and stock photos, then rely on color alone to show key differences.
questions.explanation: Brief text, relevant high-contrast visuals, and alt text make the presentation easier to read and more accessible to a wider audience.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: A student wants to establish how an edited image spread online. Which action would provide the strongest evidence of its chronology?
choices: Count the reposts of each version to determine which one appeared first.
Ask longtime users where they remember encountering the image for the first time.
Compare archived captures and platform timestamps to identify the earliest surviving version and later alterations.
Rank the versions by account popularity and color saturation to decide which one is oldest.
questions.explanation: Archived captures and timestamps provide documented evidence for when surviving versions appeared and how the image changed.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: A student is comparing a river before and after a restoration project for a multimedia report. Which plan best supports accurate visual analysis?
choices: Display only the after photograph so viewers see the improved condition.
Replace both photographs with long quotations from a local official.
Place the photographs side by side, label dates and locations, and annotate visible changes.
Combine the photographs into an unlabeled collage to create a stronger emotional effect.
questions.explanation: This plan preserves visual evidence while giving viewers the context needed to compare the documented changes.
questions.topic: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses punctuation correctly to join three related independent clauses while retaining an introductory dependent clause?
choices: After the orientation, the lecture explained the assignment; the handout listed evaluation criteria; and the sample essay showed how to cite sources.
After the orientation, the lecture explained the assignment; the handout listed evaluation criteria; and, the sample essay showed how to cite sources.
After the orientation, the lecture explained the assignment; the handout, listed evaluation criteria; and the sample essay showed how to cite sources.
After the orientation, the lecture explained the assignment; the handout listed evaluation criteria, and the sample essay showed how to cite sources.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses a comma after the introductory phrase, semicolons to separate the three independent clauses, and a comma before the final and.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: A student is building an interactive graph that lets readers change the year and compare values for several states. Which design choice best helps readers interpret the changes accurately?
choices: Let the vertical scale change automatically for every year, and display only the state with the largest selected value.
Use a different color for each year, and omit the units so the changing pattern remains visually striking.
Keep the vertical scale and units fixed for every year, and display the exact selected value and name the data source.
Sort the states differently for every year, and replace exact values with stars to encourage a quick ranking.
questions.explanation: A consistent scale and labeled units make comparisons valid, while exact values and source information keep the interactive display interpretable.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: A researcher intends to state that only the students who attended the workshop scored higher on the survey. Which sentence communicates that meaning most precisely?
choices: Only the students who attended the workshop scored higher on the survey.
The students who attended the workshop scored higher on the survey.
The students, who attended the workshop, scored higher on the survey.
Students who attended the workshop, as well as other students, scored higher on the survey.
questions.explanation: The word Only limits the claim to workshop attendees, while the unpunctuated clause who attended the workshop identifies which students are meant.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: An argument says, "Because campuses provide free tutoring, fewer students will fail." The data show that many students use tutoring. Which revision best supplies the missing logical link?
choices: If tutoring gives students help they need, then increased use of tutoring should reduce failures.
Most students who use tutoring earn passing grades, even though the program is free.
Campuses with free tutoring report lower failure rates than campuses without it.
Free tutoring programs are more common at colleges with smaller class sizes.
questions.explanation: This revision supplies the warrant by explaining why increased use of tutoring could lead to fewer course failures.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses parallel structure correctly in its three-part compound predicate?
choices: The researcher interviewed students, analyzed their responses, and compared the results with earlier surveys.
The researcher interviewed students, analyzed their responses, and a comparison with earlier surveys.
The researcher interviewed students, an analysis of their responses, and a comparison with earlier surveys.
The researcher interviewed students, analyzed their responses, and comparing the results with earlier surveys.
questions.explanation: The three coordinate verbs—interviewed, analyzed, and compared—use consistent grammatical forms and complete the compound predicate.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 9: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses parallel structure for the three actions in the assignment?
choices: Students needed to analyze a source, evaluate its evidence, and defend a position.
Students needed to analyze a source, evaluating its evidence, and defend a position.
Students needed analyzing a source, evaluate its evidence, and defend a position.
Students needed to analyze a source, evaluation of its evidence, and defend a position.
questions.explanation: The three infinitives analyze, evaluate, and defend are parallel in form and grammatical function.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: A college dean claims that first-year seminars improve retention because the seminars create supportive links to advisors and peers. Which finding would most directly test whether that explanation accounts for the retention benefit?
choices: First-year seminar participants had a higher four-year retention rate than students who never attended a seminar.
First-year seminar satisfaction ratings have risen over the past three years.
Students who reported stronger ties to both advisors and peers were more likely to remain enrolled even after seminar attendance was statistically controlled.
Students who expect to graduate are more likely to register for first-year seminars.
questions.explanation: This finding tests the proposed mechanism by connecting stronger campus relationships to retention while accounting for seminar attendance.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 9: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: A pilot tracked the same 120 students before and after a semester in which they used a reading app, and their average score increased from 72 percent to 79 percent. Which conclusion is fully supported by these results?
choices: The app caused every student's score to increase by seven percentage points.
Scores will increase by seven percentage points for all students who use the app.
Average scores rose from 72 percent to 79 percent among the pilot students during the app-use semester.
At least 120 students will improve their reading scores by seven points if they use the app.
questions.explanation: The reported averages and study period support this limited description of the pilot results without claiming causation or universal effects.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses subject-verb agreement correctly?
choices: The set of digital sources and its annotations is available in the research archive.
The set of digital sources and its annotations are available in the research archive.
The set of digital sources and its annotations were available in the research archive.
The set of digital sources and its annotations have been available in the research archive.
questions.explanation: The singular noun set is the subject, so the present-tense verb is takes the singular form is.
questions.topic: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: What should a student do to make a long PDF report navigable for readers who use assistive technology?
choices: Convert every page to a flat image and add page numbers to the bottom.
Place all text in decorative boxes and order it according to visual placement on each page.
Use properly tagged headings, alternative text for visuals, and a logical reading order.
Add one descriptive title to the cover page and let readers scroll through the document.
questions.explanation: Tagged headings, alternative text, and logical reading order communicate the report's structure and content to assistive technology.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: A study reports that 64 percent of pilot students felt more prepared after using an online planning tool. Which sentence represents the evidence accurately without claiming more than the study shows?
choices: The online planning tool caused 64 percent of pilot students to feel more prepared.
In the pilot group, 64 percent of students reported feeling more prepared after using the tool, but that reported result does not by itself establish causation.
The online planning tool was proven effective because 64 percent of the pilot group felt more prepared.
Research shows that 64 percent of students became more prepared after using the tool.
questions.explanation: This version preserves the study's reported findings and population while acknowledging that the result alone does not prove the tool caused the change.
questions.topic: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: In a college essay, which sentence integrates a study finding that teenagers averaged 7.8 hours of sleep most effectively?
choices: The researchers observed that teens averaged 7.8 hours of sleep, a figure that helps explain the concentration problems described later in the essay.
Teens averaged 7.8 hours of sleep, which is fewer than eight hours, according to one study.
The study found 7.8 hours, but some students in the writer's class may sleep much longer.
Although 7.8 hours was observed, the researchers questioned how reliably the teenagers could remember their sleep.
questions.explanation: This sentence accurately presents the finding and clearly connects its significance to the essay's later discussion.
questions.topic: Tester 9 of 9: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9

questions.prompt: A student is making a video essay that interprets a short story. Which plan best coordinates spoken commentary, visual evidence, and written text to make the interpretation clear?
choices: Read the full story aloud while unrelated landscape photographs remain behind every scene.
Display only the story's publication page and summarize the plot without quoting key passages.
Show the book's cover and discuss the author's biography before stating a claim about the story.
Display key passages as written text, read brief excerpts aloud, and connect each visual choice to a claim about theme.
questions.explanation: This plan uses all three modes purposefully by pairing textual evidence, spoken analysis, and relevant visuals to support an interpretation.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: A college applicant wants an opening that demonstrates a specific experience, thoughtful reflection, and an honest voice. Which sentence best meets all three goals?
choices: As everyone knows, a strong personal statement can determine a student's future, and I am excited to begin this important journey.
My greatest weakness is perfectionism, which I overcame by becoming the best version of myself overnight.
Although many students enjoy writing, my essay discusses a topic that truly matters to me because it is important to me.
When my debate team revised my opening statement, I learned that clarity mattered more than sounding forceful, and the experience changed how I listen.
questions.explanation: This sentence presents a concrete experience, explains the lesson the writer drew from it, and uses a personal voice without making a sweeping claim.
questions.skill: Authentic Voice and Reflective College Writing
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: A slide presents a four-step laboratory procedure. Which visual most helps an audience understand both the sequence and the branching decisions?
choices: A decorative stock photograph of a scientist holding a pipette.
A flowchart with labeled boxes for each step and arrows showing possible outcomes.
A 120-word paragraph placed in small type below the slide title.
A bar chart comparing test scores from three different classes.
questions.explanation: A flowchart makes the sequence of a procedure visible while its labeled arrows show where the process can branch.
questions.topic: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing

questions.prompt: A writer is building an argument that digital research tools can help students analyze difficult texts. Which sentence most effectively acknowledges a reasonable objection and responds to it fairly?
choices: Although some students argue that digital access can distract from difficult reading, assigning curated excerpts and short response tasks can make that access support focused analysis.
Although some students argue that digital access can distract from difficult reading, classroom technology should be expanded because every student benefits from more screens.
If students are distracted by digital access, teachers should prohibit research databases until the distraction disappears entirely.
While concerns about distraction deserve further study, access to digital research databases is valuable because it is popular with most students.
questions.explanation: This sentence presents a credible concern, directly addresses it, and offers a reasoned response rather than dismissing or exaggerating the objection.
questions.topic: Argument and Rhetoric: Concession and Rebuttal

questions.prompt: An article claims that new bus routes will improve college access because more students will be able to travel without relying on a car. Which sentence best supports the claim while acknowledging an important limitation?
choices: Ridership on the new routes rose after launch, which proves that every student near a campus can now attend college without a car.
Ridership on several new routes serving nearby campuses rose after launch, suggesting that access may have improved, though fares and schedule gaps can still prevent some students from traveling.
A few commuters said the buses were more comfortable than driving, a change that clearly guarantees equal access for all riders.
Transit agencies across the region bought more buses, proving that expanded routes will meet every student's transportation needs.
questions.explanation: This sentence offers relevant evidence without overstating its certainty and identifies fares and schedules as factors that may still limit access.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 9 of 9: Digital and Multimodal Composition through Preparing for College-Level Writing
